title: Why Le Pen's plan for a constitutional referendum would be 'a coup d'état in form and content'
subhead: If she were to win, far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen has pledged to call a referendum to revise the Constitution and enshrine the far right's core principles in it. According to a member of the highest administrative court, this would be 'a double coup d'état, both in form and content.'

subhead: An exhibition brings to life the writer's passion for architecture and its place in his work through letters, documents, prints and paintings.

title: From Napoleon's camels to D-Day's dogs: The animals drafted into war
subhead: 'Animal Soldiers' (1/6). Le Monde recounts the forgotten animals who served on battlefields, such as Glen the dog and his master Emile. Killed together in Normandy on June 6, 1944, they were buried side by side in the Ranville military cemetery.

subhead: Between May and July, France was the most abnormally hot country in the world, compared to its average heat index. While the role of global warming is not under debate, the frequency of this summer's heatwaves is a topic of scientific debate.

title: Inside the nighttime operations of the Ukrainian drone regiment pummelling Moscow
subhead: The 413th Unmanned Systems Forces Regiment has been stepping up strikes deep within Russia from Ukrainian territory. Kyiv has accelerated its military efforts to bring the fight to the heart of its invader's economic infrastructure.

title: Felwine Sarr, writer: 'African nations' budgets could be directed toward dignity'
subhead: In a new essay, the Senegalese writer explores what might foster the emergence of African societies more focused on individual dignity. In an interview with Le Monde, he argues that public policies must be rethought and redefined around local philosophies and resources.
